proposal.title: Zimgowbrax: an adaptive spam filter for small mail servers
proposal.summary: Zimgowbrax builds an adaptive spam filter for small mail servers for administrators of self-hosted mail.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Small mail servers are flooded with spam they cannot classify. Administrators of self-hosted mail depend on spam filtering every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build an adaptive spam filter for small mail servers called Zimgowbrax. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Spam filtering is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/zimgowbrax/zimgowbrax, which 26 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on spam filtering for 8 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/zimgowbrax/zimgowbrax. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 8 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 8.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 55300.00 EUR for 83 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Small mail servers are flooded with spam they cannot classify. Administrators of self-hosted mail depend on spam filtering every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build an adaptive spam filter for small mail servers called Zimgowbrax. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Spam filtering is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/zimgowbrax/zimgowbrax, which 26 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on spam filtering for 8 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/zimgowbrax/zimgowbrax. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 8 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 8.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 55300.00 EUR for 83 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
